title: Library map
transcript: The library has three places to read. The quiet corner is beside the window. The round table is for partners. Try the back rug if you want to listen to a story.
task: Where should you go to read with a partner?

title: Seedlings
transcript: Two groups planted bean seeds. Both groups gave their seeds the same amount of water. The seeds near the window sprouted first. More light might have helped the seedlings grow once they sprouted, but this test does not show why the first seeds sprouted sooner.
task: What did both groups keep the same?

title: Missing mitten
transcript: At recess, a child noticed that one mitten was missing. First, they checked under the slide. Then they remembered rolling a snowball near the fence. They found the mitten beside a small pile of snow.
task: What clue helped the child know where to look next?

title: Classroom pet
transcript: Our class should watch birds outside instead of getting a classroom pet. We can still observe how animals behave, but no one has to care for an animal when school is closed.
task: What reason does the speaker give for watching birds?

title: Reuse bin
transcript: The reuse bin holds paper that is blank on one side. Take a sheet when you need to draw or solve a problem. When you have used both sides, put the sheet in the recycling bin.
task: When should a sheet go in the recycling bin?

title: Rain garden
transcript: A rain garden sits lower than the sidewalk. After heavy rain, water flows into the garden and collects there. The soil absorbs some of the water over time. This helps slow the flow of water into the storm drain.
task: How does the garden help slow water flowing into the storm drain?

title: Later bus
transcript: The school should test a later activity bus twice a week. Some students cannot stay for clubs because they need a ride home. A short trial would let the school count riders before committing to a full schedule.
task: Why does the speaker propose a trial?

title: Lunch survey
transcript: The lunch survey asked students to pick the name of one meal they would order again. Forty out of sixty students selected the rice bowl. The survey recorded preferences among the people who answered. It did not measure how much food anyone ate.

title: Broken model
transcript: Our science model collapsed just before the demonstration. We first tried adding tape, but the frame still leaned. A teammate suggested making the base wider. We tested that change, and the frame stayed upright long enough to present.

title: Drink ratios
transcript: One recipe uses two cups of concentrate and three cups of water. Another uses four cups of concentrate and six cups of water. The second recipe doubles both amounts, so the amount of concentrate for each cup of water stays the same.
task: Why should the two drinks taste equally strong?

title: Shadow
transcript: My shadow moved because the Sun appeared in a different part of the sky. The light came from a new direction, so my shadow pointed a different way.
task: Why did the shadow point a different way?
followup: The light came from a new direction.

title: Paper
transcript: The folded paper held more coins because the folds helped it keep its shape. The flat paper bent sooner when we put coins on it.
task: Explain why the folded paper held more coins.
followup: What does the flat paper tell us that the folded paper alone would not?

title: Read outside
transcript: Our class should try reading outside on Friday. We can choose a quiet spot, and students who need shade can sit under the tree.
task: Should the class try reading outside?
followup: Connect one reason directly to how students would benefit.

title: Jug
transcript: I think we should bring a refillable water jug to field day. Everyone can refill a bottle, so we will need fewer single-use cups.
task: What should the class bring to field day?
followup: Name what you would bring and explain what it would change.

title: Histogram
transcript: The tallest bar shows that more students read for twenty to twenty-nine minutes than for any other interval. A histogram groups times into ranges, so this bar does not tell me the exact number of minutes each student read.
task: Explain what the tallest bar tells you and what it leaves unknown.
followup: Use the term interval and contrast a group with an individual measurement.

title: Variable
transcript: The number of notebooks is the independent variable because the buyer chooses it. The total cost is the dependent variable because it changes with the number of notebooks.
task: Which quantity depends on the other?
followup: Name both quantities and say how one changes with the other.

title: Courtyard
transcript: The school should add shade to the courtyard before adding more seats. If the seats are too hot at lunch, adding more of them will not make the space comfortable to use.
task: Should a school add courtyard shade or more seating first?
followup: Explain why your priority solves a problem the other choice leaves open.

title: Device
transcript: The class should keep a paper copy of the directions for group work. A digital copy is easy to update, but a paper copy lets the group keep working if the device runs out of power.
task: Should groups have access to paper directions too?
followup: Acknowledge one strength of the other option, then explain your choice.

title: Listen, pause, and explain
transcript: For this optional practice, listen to the example first. Then pause and explain your thinking out loud. Try using the word because to connect your idea to a reason. Listen again if you need to, and give your explanation one more try.

title: Escucha, haz una pausa y explica
transcript: Para esta práctica opcional, escucha primero el ejemplo. Luego, haz una pausa y explica en voz alta cómo pensaste. Usa la palabra porque para conectar tu idea con una razón. Si lo necesitas, escucha el ejemplo otra vez y vuelve a explicar tu respuesta.

title: Choose a starting point
transcript: Pick any activity that feels manageable today. If the directions are new, try the first example together. Stop after one short practice round, or keep going if you want to.

title: Elige por dónde empezar
transcript: Elige una actividad que te parezca adecuada para hoy. Si las instrucciones son nuevas, prueben juntos el primer ejemplo. Pueden parar después de una ronda corta o seguir si quieren.

title: Listen for a detail
transcript: Listen once for the main idea. Then replay the clip and listen for one detail that supports it. You can tell someone the detail or point to it in the transcript.

title: Escucha para encontrar un detalle
transcript: Escucha una vez para identificar la idea principal. Luego, vuelve a escuchar el audio y presta atención a un detalle que apoye esa idea. Puedes contarle el detalle a alguien o señalarlo en la transcripción.

title: Talk it through
transcript: You can talk about the idea in the language you use at home. When you are ready, try one sentence in English. It is fine to look at the example while you practice.

title: Conversa sobre tu idea
transcript: Puedes conversar sobre la idea en el idioma que usas en casa. Cuando estés listo, prueba decir una oración en inglés. Está bien mirar el ejemplo mientras practicas.

title: Give one helpful cue
transcript: After your child explains, name one part you understood. Then ask one short question, such as, What made you think that? Give them time to try the explanation again.

title: Da una sugerencia concreta
transcript: Después de que tu hijo o hija explique su idea, menciona una parte que entendiste. Luego haz una pregunta breve, como: ¿Qué te hizo pensar eso? Dale tiempo para volver a explicar su idea.

title: End with one small win
transcript: Before you finish, say one thing you can do better now. Maybe you caught a detail, used a new word, or gave a clearer reason. One short round of optional practice is enough for today.

title: Termina reconociendo un logro
transcript: Antes de terminar, menciona algo que ahora puedes hacer mejor. Tal vez identificaste un detalle, usaste una palabra nueva o diste una razón más clara. Una ronda corta de práctica opcional es suficiente por hoy.
